statement.text:
For any partition of an arbitrary group G into finitely many subsets G =
A1 ∪ · · · ∪ An , there exists a subset of the partition Ai and a finite subset F ⊆ G, such
that G = A−1  i Ai F (I. V. Protasov, Siberian Math. J., 34, no. 5 (1993), 938–952). Can
the subset F always be chosen so that |F | ⩽ n? This is true for amenable groups.
                                                                            I. V. Protasov
